childNodes.textContent: In any such mixture where there is overlapping, it will be obvious that every one of these mixtures is lighter than any of the mixture parents.
Your screen is three kinds of light, red, green and blue. Drag them over each other. Where two overlap you get a lighter colour, and where all three meet you get white.

childNodes.textContent: On the contrary, the more color that is mixed, the more the mixture approaches a dark grey leaning toward black.
Inks work the other way. Each one takes some light away from the white paper, so every overlap is darker than either ink. All three together come close to black.

childNodes.textContent: Light added to light always gets lighter, and all three together make white
Paint or ink mixed with paint always gets darker, heading towards black
Mixing in the eye, as on a spinning disc, lands between the two
A screen is literally additive light. Print is subtractive ink
Colours that work on screen can turn muddy in print, so check both before handing over a palette
